implementation_statement: Access Control Policy POL-02 and standards STD-02.1 to STD-02.4 (P06) apply to the TDPB. Procedures cover provisioning, quarterly certification, privileged access, vendor access, and OT shared-account handling.

Corporate and OT accounts for CAD, PTC back office, and CTC code servers are provisioned through identity governance from HR events and role templates approved by the Vice President, Network Operations and the Director of Train Control Systems. Quarterly certifications cover all TDPB roles. Gap: at AQ-04 to AQ-06 terminations are processed manually in local directories, and 3 of 60 sampled terminations were disabled 2 to 9 days late (POAM-001).
evidence: Identity governance role templates; CAD and PTC user exports; P07 AC-2 results

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Joiner, mover, and leaver events flow automatically from the HR system to identity governance, which provisions and removes TDPB roles in the corporate and OT directories.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Accounts inactive for 45 days are disabled automatically in both directories; dispatcher accounts on extended leave are suspended by the NOC.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Account creation, change, and removal in the corporate and OT directories and in the CAD and PTC applications are logged and forwarded to the SIEM.

CAD enforces role-based permissions by desk and territory (a dispatcher can issue authority only on assigned territories); the PTC back office enforces roles for train control technicians, key custodians, and SL-1 tenant users. Gap: a legacy two-way trust between the corporate and OT directories lets 2 corporate groups resolve permissions on OT servers; the trust has never been reviewed (POAM-005).
evidence: CAD role matrix; PTC role matrix; directory trust export; P07 AC-3 results

implementation_statement: Traffic between the corporate network, the industrial DMZ, and the NOC operations zone is limited to documented flows (TMS consists, crew data, SIEM forwarding, vendor PAM sessions). OT services do not traverse the corporate network except through the industrial DMZ brokers.
evidence: Firewall rule base; zone and conduit diagram; flow register

implementation_statement: Duties are separated: dispatchers issue authority but cannot change territory tables or CAD configuration; the CAD and PTC configuration teams cannot issue authority; PTC key custodians are separate from server administrators.
Least privilege: administrators use separate privileged accounts checked out from PAM for each session; dispatch consoles run as standard users in a locked-down shell.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Security functions (firewall, PAM, EDR, directory administration) are authorized to named security and infrastructure roles only.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Administrators use non-privileged accounts for email and web; privileged accounts cannot log on to office endpoints.
evidence: Directory tiering policy; logon restriction GPOs

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Privileged accounts for TDPB servers are restricted to 31 named administrators and vaulted in PAM.
evidence: Privileged account list; PAM vault inventory

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: PAM records every privileged session with keystroke and video capture; recordings are kept 1 year.

SSO locks accounts after 10 failed attempts in 15 minutes. Dispatch consoles use a dispatcher-specific rule (lockout replaced by supervisor alert) so a dispatcher is never locked out mid-shift; the alternative is documented under SD Sec. III.C.1.b.
evidence: SSO policy; console alert rule; CIP mitigation entry

implementation_statement: CAD, PTC, and CTC logon screens show the approved system use notice, including that the system contains SSI.

Administrator workstations lock after 15 minutes. Dispatch consoles do not lock during a shift (operational necessity); they are in the badge-controlled NOC floor and the exception is documented (EXC-2026-007).
Administrative web sessions to CAD and PTC consoles end after 30 minutes idle; dispatcher sessions end at shift change.

control_name: Permitted Actions Without Identification or Authentication
implementation_statement: No CAD, PTC, or CTC function is available without identification except the read-only NOC wall display, which shows train positions only.

Remote administration and vendor support for CAD, PTC, and CTC go through the PAM gateway with MFA, approval per session, and recording. Gap: the crossing monitor vendor reaches about 310 crossing monitors through its own cellular modems outside PAM, and 2 of those modems also reach a CTC field code unit network in the Central region (POAM-008).
evidence: PAM gateway configuration; vendor access register; P07 AC-17 results

implementation_statement: Remote sessions through PAM and the remote access service are monitored by the SOC with alerts for off-hours vendor sessions.

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: Remote access uses TLS 1.2 or higher; vendor sessions are proxied and never terminate directly on OT hosts.
Wireless is not permitted in the NOC operations zone; corporate Wi-Fi at the NOCs is on the corporate network only and scanned monthly for rogue access points.
Mobile devices may not connect to the NOC operations zone; crew tablets reach CAD bulletins only through the published bulletin service in the industrial DMZ.
Use of external systems to process TDPB data is limited to approved vendor portals and the SL-1 and SL-2 customer interfaces under contract (STD-02.3).
Security awareness and training standard STD-05.1 sets annual, role-based, and new-hire training, including TSA security training for security-sensitive employees.
All workforce complete annual awareness training and monthly phishing simulations; NOC staff complete an OT-specific module.
Awareness training covers insider threat indicators and how to report them to the rail security department.

Role-based training: dispatchers and NOC supervisors complete annual cyber incident and manual operations training; administrators complete OT security training. Gap: 81% of dispatchers completed the 2026 module by 2026-07-31 against a 100% target (POAM-016).
evidence: Learning system reports; P07 AT-3 results

implementation_statement: Audit logging standard STD-01.4 applies, including OT log sources and retention for investigation.

Logged events: authority issued, changed, voided, and released; territory table changes; PTC configuration and key events; logons; privileged sessions; configuration changes; and security alerts from consoles and servers.
Records include time, user, console, territory, train, event type, and outcome.
evidence: Sample CAD and PTC audit records

implementation_statement: CAD authority records also store the authority text and the conflict-check result.
SIEM storage is sized for 13 months online; capacity alerts at 75%.

control_name: Response to Audit Logging Process Failures
implementation_statement: The SIEM alerts the SOC when a TDPB log source stops sending for 60 minutes.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The SOC reviews TDPB alerts continuously and the CAD and PTC teams review authority and configuration exception reports weekly. Gap: the SIEM receives 61% of OT log sources; CTC code servers, 41 field code unit gateways, and the PTC message brokers are not forwarded (POAM-007).
evidence: SOC case records; weekly review records; log source inventory; P07 AU-6 results

implementation_statement: Correlation and alerting are automated in the SIEM and the SOAR platform.
OT network detection, EDR, PAM, and SIEM records are correlated in one SOC case view.
All TDPB components synchronize to redundant internal time sources traceable to a national time standard; PTC components use the PTC system time source.
Logs forwarded to the SIEM are write-once in the log archive; administrators of CAD and PTC cannot delete SIEM records.

control_name: Access by Subset of Privileged Users
implementation_statement: Only 6 SOC engineers can manage SIEM retention settings.
SIEM records are kept 13 months online and 7 years in the archive. Gap: sources not forwarded to the SIEM (CTC code servers, PTC message brokers) keep only 30 days locally (POAM-007).
Audit generation is enabled on all CAD and PTC servers and consoles; the SIEM agent configuration is part of the server baseline.
Security assessment standard STD-01.2 covers assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring, aligned to the TSA Cybersecurity Assessment Plan.
Internal Audit assesses TDPB controls annually; the Cybersecurity Assessment Plan schedules at least one third of the CIP measures each year and all of them over 3 years.
evidence: P07 plan and report; Cybersecurity Assessment Plan schedule

implementation_statement: Assessors are independent of the teams that design and operate the controls (Internal Audit, co-sourced OT specialists).
Interconnections with Class I and passenger operators, the industry messaging network, SL-1 and SL-2 customers, and the TMS are documented in interconnection agreements with security terms.
Weaknesses from assessments, the TSA assessment report, and the architecture design review are tracked in the POA&M with owners and dates (P07).
The Chief Operating Officer is the authorizing official equivalent and granted conditional authorization on 2026-09-14 (SSP section 4.2).
Continuous monitoring: monthly metrics on patch age, log coverage, privileged sessions, and vendor access; quarterly reporting to the executive risk committee.
Internal connections between CAD, PTC, CTC code servers, and the NOC consoles are documented in the zone and conduit model with allowed protocols.
Configuration and change management standard STD-01.5 and change procedure PRC-01.3 apply, including the PTC change rules required by 49 CFR 236.1023(c).
Hardened baselines exist for CAD servers, PTC servers, CTC code servers, and dispatch consoles; deviations are reported weekly.

control_name: Automation Support for Accuracy and Currency
implementation_statement: Baseline compliance is scanned automatically every week.
Two prior baselines and the vendor-certified images are retained for rollback.

Changes go through the operations change board, with vendor certification for PTC software (236.1023) and a dispatcher acceptance test for CAD territory changes. Gap: 3 of 40 sampled CAD emergency changes had no retrospective approval within 2 business days (POAM-011).

control_name: Testing, Validation, and Documentation of Changes
implementation_statement: Changes are tested in the CAD and PTC lab environments before production.
Security impact analysis is part of each change record; changes that add Critical Cyber Systems trigger a CIP amendment check (SD Sec. VI.B).
Only change-approved PAM sessions can modify production; direct administrator logons are blocked.

Configuration settings follow vendor hardening guides and CIS-derived settings where the vendor certifies them. Gap: USB storage was enabled on 9 of 148 dispatch consoles at the backup NOC (POAM-017).
Only required services run on CAD, PTC, and CTC servers; application allowlisting is enforced on dispatch consoles and servers.
Ports and services are reviewed quarterly against the zone and conduit model.

The CMDB holds TDPB servers, consoles, network devices, and PTC components, reconciled monthly with network discovery. Gap: the wider OT inventory is 88% complete; about 310 vendor-installed crossing monitors and their modems are missing (POAM-009).
evidence: CMDB; discovery reports; P07 CM-8 results

implementation_statement: Inventory is updated as part of each installation and removal change.
Software is licensed and tracked; PTC and CAD software is used under vendor license with escrow.
Users cannot install software on dispatch consoles or servers; allowlisting blocks unapproved code.
Contingency and disaster recovery standard STD-03.3 applies.

The TDPB contingency plan (v6) sets roles, RTO and RPO from the BIA (P05), failover to DC-2, and manual dispatch procedures. Gap: the plan has no tested procedure to answer a TSA RSSM location request if the TMS is down (POAM-019), and the crew calling telephony fallback is untested (POAM-021).
evidence: TDPB contingency plan v6; P07 CP-2 results

implementation_statement: The plan is coordinated with the Class I and passenger operators (interchange and operating agreements) and with SL-1 and SL-2 customer notices.
Mission essential functions (movement authority, PTC on host segments, TSA location answers) resume within the BIA times.
Critical assets are identified in the BIA and the CIP Critical Cyber System list.
Dispatchers and the train control team are trained annually on their contingency roles.

The DR test runs annually (last 2026-04-25) and tabletop exercises test at least two Incident Response Plan objectives a year. Gap: the manual dispatch fallback for CTC territory has been exercised at 2 of 11 signaled railroads (POAM-020).
evidence: DR test report; exercise reports; P07 CP-4 results

implementation_statement: Tests are coordinated with the Class I dispatch centers and passenger operators affected.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Data center and cloud platform
implementation_statement: Backups are copied to separate immutable backup accounts and to an offline copy in DC-2.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Data center and cloud platform
implementation_statement: DC-2 in Texas and the backup NOC are the alternate processing and operations sites.

Diverse carriers serve DC-1, DC-2, and both NOCs; radio backhaul has cellular backup at 210 of about 380 sites. Gap: 14 tower sites on CTC territory have one route, and the crew calling telephony provider has no tested alternative (POAM-021).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Data center and cloud platform
implementation_statement: CAD and PTC databases are backed up every 15 minutes (log shipping) and daily (full); backups are encrypted, immutable for 35 days, and scanned with host security software when made and when restored.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Data center and cloud platform
implementation_statement: Restores are tested quarterly for CAD and PTC databases.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Data center and cloud platform
implementation_statement: Backups are encrypted with keys held in the backup account key service.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Data center and cloud platform
implementation_statement: CAD recovers by automatic failover to DC-2 (1.6 hours in the 2026-04-25 test, RTO 2 hours). Gap: the PTC back office failover is manual and took 9.5 hours against a 4-hour RTO (POAM-006).
evidence: DR test report; P07 CP-10 results

implementation_statement: CAD replicates authority transactions synchronously to DC-2, so recovery keeps every authority in effect.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Identification and authentication standard STD-02.2 applies, including the memorized secret reset criteria required by SD Sec. III.C.1.a.

Users are uniquely identified in the corporate or OT directory. Gap: the CTC code servers use 3 shared administrator accounts whose passwords were not changed when 2 signal engineers left in 2026 (POAM-004).
evidence: Directory exports; CTC account list; P07 IA-2 results

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Privileged access to TDPB servers needs phishing-resistant MFA through PAM.

Non-privileged remote access needs MFA. Dispatch consoles on the badge-controlled NOC floor use a badge tap plus password; this compensating control for MFA in OT is documented in the CIP (Sec. III.C.2).

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Authentication protocols resist replay (Kerberos with AES, TLS, FIDO2).
Onboard PTC apparatus and wayside interface units authenticate to the back office with cryptographic credentials managed under the PTC key management procedure (49 CFR 236.1033).
evidence: Key management procedure; device credential list

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Identifiers are assigned by identity governance and never reused.

Passwords meet STD-02.2 (length 14, banned list, reset only on evidence of compromise per SP 800-63B, as SD Sec. III.C.1.a footnote 9 points to). Gap: testing found vendor default credentials on 4 wayside detector modems and 2 field code unit gateways (POAM-012).
evidence: STD-02.2; credential test results; P07 IA-5 results

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Password checks against breached-password lists are enforced in both directories.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Certificate-based authentication for servers and PTC components chains to the company and PTC certificate authorities.
SL-2 customer dispatchers and SL-1 customer technicians sign in with federated or company-issued accounts with MFA; each customer administrator attests quarterly.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Re-authentication is required for privileged elevation and after 12 hours.
Incident response and resilience policy POL-03 and standards STD-03.1 to STD-03.3 apply.
SOC, NOC supervisors, and the train control team complete annual incident response training.

The Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan is exercised at least annually, testing at least two of the objectives in SD 1580-21-01E Sec. II.D.1 with the positions named in the plan (2026-03-18 exercise tested isolation and backup integrity).
The SOC handles incidents with SOAR playbooks; the NOC and train control team join for OT incidents; IT/OT isolation steps are pre-approved (P08).
SOAR automates enrichment, containment of endpoints, and case creation.
Incidents are tracked to closure in SOC case management.

Reportable incidents are reported to CISA within the 72 hours set by SD 1580-21-01E Sec. II.C.2 (company target 24 hours, so the same report also meets 1570.203), to TSA TSOC within 12 hours as recommended by IC Surface-2025-01, and through the P08 matrix.
An incident response retainer and the MSSP provide assistance; outside counsel and forensics are on retainer.

The Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan names positions and resources and covers isolation, offline backups, and IT/OT isolation. Gap: the SEC materiality steps and the TSA/CISA steps sit in separate playbooks, and the disclosure committee has not exercised them since 3 members joined (POAM-010).
evidence: Incident Response Plan; playbooks; P07 IR-8 results

implementation_statement: Maintenance standard STD-01.6 applies.
Maintenance of CAD, PTC, and CTC components follows the PTCSP maintenance procedures and vendor schedules; records are kept with change tickets.
Nonlocal maintenance by CAD and PTC vendors uses PAM with MFA, approval, and recording; sessions end when work ends.
Vendor engineers who work on site are escorted in the data centers and NOCs; remote vendor engineers are named in the vendor access register.
Media protection and disposal standard STD-04.2 applies, including SSI marking and destruction.
Media containing SSI (CIP, assessment results) is restricted to the SSI library and named holders.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Data center and cloud platform
implementation_statement: Media leaving the data centers is wiped to NIST SP 800-88 or destroyed with certificates.
Removable media is blocked on servers and consoles except approved, scanned media for vendor-certified updates.
Physical security standard STD-01.7 applies to the NOCs and data centers.
NOC and data center access lists are approved by the Director, Network Operations Center and reviewed quarterly.
Badge plus PIN at the NOC floor and data halls; mantrap at DC-1; railroad police patrols.
CCTV and alarms are monitored 24/7 by the railroad police communications center.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Data center and cloud platform
implementation_statement: DC-1, DC-2, and both NOCs have UPS and generators (96 hours of fuel at DC-1).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Data center and cloud platform
implementation_statement: Data halls have clean-agent fire suppression with monitored detection.
Planning is governed by POL-01 and the policy hierarchy (P06).
This SSP describes the TDPB and is kept consistent with the TSA-approved CIP, which incorporates it by reference (SD Sec. IV.A).
Users accept the acceptable use policy POL-05 annually; NOC staff also acknowledge SSI handling rules.
Baseline: SP 800-53B Moderate, with High-baseline supplements for integrity and availability (section 6).
Tailoring decisions are recorded in this SSP and approved by the authorizing official.
Personnel security procedures are in the HR program and POL-01.
Background checks for all hires; dispatchers, train control staff, and administrators get an enhanced check.
Terminations remove access through identity governance the same business day. Gap: at AQ-04 to AQ-06 removal is manual from local directories (POAM-001).
Transfers trigger an access review by the new manager within 10 days.
TDPB users sign the access agreement and SSI non-disclosure acknowledgment.
Sanctions follow PRC-01.1 and collective bargaining agreement discipline procedures.
Risk assessment standard STD-01.1 applies (SP 800-30 Rev. 1; NIST IR 8286 Rev. 1).
The TDPB is categorized in section 6 using FIPS 199 as a model.
The annual enterprise risk analysis (P01) covers the TDPB; risks roll up to the enterprise register.
Supply chain risks for the CAD and PTC vendors and the messaging network are assessed annually.

Credentialed vulnerability scans run weekly on IT components; OT components are covered by passive network detection and quarterly active scans in maintenance windows. Gap: 22% of wayside and field components are outside passive detection coverage (POAM-014).
evidence: Scan reports; coverage report; P07 RA-5 results

implementation_statement: Vulnerability feeds, including the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, update daily.
Risk responses are recorded in the risk register and POA&M.
Criticality analysis identifies the Critical Cyber Systems (CAD, PTC back office, CTC code servers, NOC operations zone) and their supporting components.
Contracts for CAD, PTC, and CTC products include security requirements, vulnerability notification, and the 236.1023 failure notification terms.

External services are tiered and reviewed (SOC reports, questionnaires); MSSP and vendor duties are mapped to the CIP so the company keeps responsibility (SD Sec. II.A.2). Gap: SOC report reviews are overdue for 14 of 140 tier-1 vendors, including the crew calling telephony provider (POAM-015).
CAD and PTC vendors use configuration management with signed releases; the company verifies signatures before installation.
Vendor releases are tested in the company lab with regression and safety test suites before production.
No unsupported components remain in the TDPB boundary; legacy components at AQ-04 to AQ-06 are outside the boundary and tracked for migration.
System and communications protection is covered by POL-04 and STD-04.1 and the network standards.
Upstream DDoS protection covers internet-facing customer services; the NOC operations zone has no internet exposure.

The NOC operations zone sits behind the industrial DMZ; boundaries deny by default and block known malicious addresses and Tor exit nodes. Gap: a test from an AQ-06 site network reached TMS integration APIs in Cloud provider A through a legacy site VPN (POAM-018).
External connections to the TDPB are limited to 7 managed access points in the industrial DMZ.
Each external connection has a documented interface agreement and is reviewed annually.

control_name: Deny by Default: Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Deny by default, allow by exception at every zone boundary.
Split tunneling is disabled for remote access to the TDPB.

CAD, PTC, and TMS traffic is encrypted in transit; PTC wireless messages carry cryptographic integrity and authentication (236.1033(a)). Gap: CTC code line traffic between code servers and field code units crosses leased carrier circuits on 3 Class II railroads without encryption or another integrity protection (POAM-013).
evidence: TLS scan; code line design; P07 SC-8 results

implementation_statement: Cryptographic protection uses TLS 1.2 or higher and IPsec between data centers.
Administrative network sessions end after 30 minutes idle.

PTC keys are generated in hardware security modules, distributed under the key management procedure, revoked on compromise or algorithm end of life, and protected from disclosure (236.1033(b)-(d)). Only 2 trained key custodians today; a third is in training (POAM-006 milestone).
evidence: Key management procedure; key ceremony records

implementation_statement: NIST-approved algorithms are used for PTC message authentication and for TLS (236.1033(b)(1)).

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Certificates come from the company PKI and the PTC certificate authority under certificate policies.
PTC sessions use authenticated messages; CAD sessions use mutually authenticated TLS between consoles and servers.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Data center and cloud platform
implementation_statement: CAD and PTC databases and backups are encrypted at rest.
System and information integrity is covered by STD-01.5 and the patch standard.

Patches follow the risk-based patch strategy: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities first, then by severity, with vendor certification for CAD and PTC. CAD servers are current. Gap: PTC back office servers are 7 months behind because the vendor certifies patches slowly, and the compensating measures required by SD Sec. III.E.3 are not documented (POAM-003).
evidence: Patch reports; vendor certification records; P07 SI-2 results

implementation_statement: Patch status is reported automatically every week.
EDR runs on all TDPB servers and consoles in vendor-certified mode; email and web defenses block malicious content enterprise-wide.

The SOC monitors TDPB with EDR, SIEM, and OT network detection at the NOC zones and DMZ, and audits OT communications that deviate from the baseline. Gap: OT network detection covers 78% of wayside and field segments, and 39% of OT log sources are not in the SIEM (POAM-007; POAM-014).

control_name: Automated Tools and Mechanisms for Real-time Analysis
implementation_statement: Automated analysis in the SIEM and SOAR supports near real-time response.
Inbound and outbound traffic at the DMZ is inspected for command-and-control patterns.
The SOC receives CISA, TSA, and rail sector alerts and vendor advisories and tracks actions.
File integrity monitoring covers CAD and PTC binaries and territory tables; CAD validates territory table checksums at load.
Integrity checks run at startup and every hour.
CAD validates authority requests against territory, limits, and conflicts before issue; PTC validates consist and track data before initialization.
CAD authority records and PTC records are retained per the PTCSP and 236.1037; SSI is handled under 1520.9.
The supply chain risk management plan covers OT vendors, including the PTC product vendor list required by 236.1023(a).
evidence: SCRM plan; PTC product vendor list

implementation_statement: Supply chain controls include signed releases, approved sources, and vendor notification duties.
Acquisition strategies prefer vendors that publish SBOMs and support certified patching cycles.
Tier-1 OT vendors are assessed annually (CAD, PTC, CTC, crossing monitor vendors); the 2026 assessments of the CAD and PTC vendors were completed.
PTC and CTC spare parts come only from the vendors on the PTC product vendor list.

control_name: Store on Separate Physical Systems or Components
implementation_statement: Audit records are stored in the log archive in Cloud provider B, separate from the TDPB systems.
Independent penetration testing of IT systems with red and purple team exercises each year, plus the architecture design review every two years (2024-06 and 2026-05).

control_name: Automated Documentation, Notification, and Prohibition of Changes
implementation_statement: Change workflow blocks deployment without approval for CAD territory tables; PTC configuration changes are approved manually. Automated blocking for PTC is planned with the PTC tooling upgrade (2027-03-31).
Changes are analyzed in separate test environments (CAD lab and PTC lab) before production.

control_name: Automated Access Enforcement and Audit Records
implementation_statement: Access restrictions for change are enforced by PAM and audited weekly.

The plan provides for continuing movement authority with minimal loss through the DC-2 standby and manual dispatch. Partially implemented: manual operations for CTC territory are not yet exercised at 9 of 11 signaled railroads (POAM-020).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Data center and cloud platform
implementation_statement: DC-2 is prepared as an operational alternate site: CAD runs hot, CTC code servers run active-active, and the PTC back office has warm standby.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Data center and cloud platform
implementation_statement: Copies of CAD and PTC system software and configurations are kept in the offline vault in DC-2.
Automated restoration of the PTC back office from configuration-controlled images within the RTO is planned with POAM-006 (2027-03-31).
CAD, PTC, and CTC components are in separate enclaves inside the NOC operations zone.
Integrity violations on CAD and PTC components alert the SOC and the on-call engineer automatically.
Automatic switchover to DC-2 on a detected integrity violation of territory tables is planned for the 2027 CAD release (2027-06-30).
